pins.head: COUNT THE PATCHES
pins.title: Acne Patches: Compare Size, Count and Cost per Patch
pins.desc: A box with more patches is not automatically cheaper if half of them are the wrong size. Count how many of each size a sheet actually gives you, then divide the price by the ones you would really use. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: Two sheets of hydrocolloid patches in mixed sizes on a white bathroom counter beside a wooden drawer, with the headline Count the Patches.

pins.head: UNDER THE BED IS A DRAWER
pins.title: Small Bedroom Organization: Treat Under the Bed as a Drawer
pins.desc: The floor under a bed is the largest empty volume in a small bedroom and it is usually holding dust. Measure the clearance first, then buy flat cases that slide out from the side you can actually reach. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: A small bedroom with a low wooden bed under a bright window, a nightstand holding a phone stand, a basket on the floor beside the rug and framed art above the bed, with the headline Under the Bed Is a Drawer.

pins.head: SIX TUBES IS ENOUGH
pins.title: An Acrylic Starter Palette: Six Tubes Cover Almost Everything
pins.desc: A large set is mostly colours you will never reach for. Two blues, two reds, a yellow and a white mix nearly anything, and learning to mix them teaches more than owning forty tubes ever will. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: A craft table with a few acrylic paint tubes and a mixing palette, with the headline Six Tubes Is Enough.

pins.head: BAGS OR PODS, DO THE MATH
pins.title: Coffee Bags or Pods: Work It Out by the Cup, Not the Pack
pins.desc: A bag and a pod box are priced on different units, so the shelf tells you nothing. Work out cups per week, divide each option by its cup count, and buy the quantity you finish while it is still fresh. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: A kraft coffee bag standing beside a stack of coloured coffee pods and a calculator on a bright kitchen counter, with the headline Bags or Pods, Do the Math.

pins.head: THE DOOR IS A WALL
pins.title: Small Bathroom Storage With No Drilling: Use the Door
pins.desc: The back of the bathroom door is the largest unused surface in the room, and it takes hooks without a single hole. Hang what you reach for daily there and keep the counter for what you use wet. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: A small rental bathroom with over-the-door hooks holding towels, a slim rolling cart beside the toilet and a plant on the window ledge, with the headline The Door Is a Wall.

pins.head: THE CLOCK STARTS AT MIXING
pins.title: An Epoxy Resin Workstation: Lay It Out Before You Mix
pins.desc: Once the two parts meet you have one working window and no time to go looking for a cup. Lay out cups, sticks, gloves and a level surface first, cover what you cannot wipe, and follow the product instructions for ventilation. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: Two clear mixing cups, two resin bottles, wooden stir sticks and blue gloves laid out on a black mat at a sunlit wooden table with plants behind, with the headline The Clock Starts at Mixing.

pins.head: WATER IS HEAVY TO SHIP
pins.title: Laundry Detergent Formats: Compare by the Load, Not the Bottle
pins.desc: Liquid is mostly water, and you pay to ship it. Compare formats by cost per load rather than by bottle size, and check the load count on the label rather than the number on the front. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: A detergent jug, a box of laundry sheets and a jar of pacs beside folded towels on a laundry shelf, with the headline Water Is Heavy to Ship.

pins.head: VERTICAL BEFORE WIDER
pins.title: Small Kitchen Organization: Go Vertical Before You Buy Wider
pins.desc: A cramped kitchen is usually short on stacked height, not floor area. Add a shelf inside the cabinet, hang what has a handle, and stand trays on edge before you buy another wide organizer. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: A narrow galley kitchen with an open green shelf of stacked bowls and mugs, a mesh bag and utensils on wall hooks, and a red pot on the stove, with the headline Vertical Before Wider.

pins.head: MEDIUM TACK DOES IT ALL
pins.title: Medium-Tack Transfer Tape for Everyday Vinyl Decals
pins.desc: High tack lifts the surface underneath and low tack drops the fine cuts. Medium tack is the one roll that handles most decals, and a grid printed on it saves squaring the design by eye. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: A cut vinyl decal and a burnishing tool on a green cutting mat at a bright workbench, with the headline Medium Tack Does It All.

pins.head: THE JAR OUTLASTS THE CREAM
pins.title: A Moisturizer Refill Routine: Buy on a Cadence, Not on Empty
pins.desc: Skin care runs out mid-week and gets replaced with whatever is nearest. Work out how many weeks a jar actually lasts, set the reorder a week before that, and the routine stops depending on a last-minute shelf. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: An open jar of cream and a standing refill pouch on a bright bathroom counter beside folded towels and a small plant, with the headline The Jar Outlasts the Cream.

pins.head: HANG TWICE, FOLD LESS
pins.title: Tiny Closet for Renters: Double the Hanging Before You Fold
pins.desc: Most rental closets waste two feet of air under the shirts. A second rod hung from the first doubles the short-garment space without a drill, and folding drops to the things that should be folded. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: An open closet with a single rod of hanging shirts and jackets, labelled storage boxes on the shelf above and a low shoe rack below, with the headline Hang Twice, Fold Less.

pins.head: A KIT, NOT A SHOPPING LIST
pins.sub: Resin Starter Kit With Coaster Molds
pins.title: An Epoxy Resin Starter Kit That Includes the Coaster Molds
pins.desc: Buying resin, hardener, cups, sticks and molds separately is where a first project stalls. A kit that ships the coaster molds alongside the resin gets the first pour done, and you learn what to buy properly afterwards. Follow the product instructions for mixing ratio and cure time. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: Hands easing a cured amber resin disc out of a round silicone mold on a black work mat, with two finished amber coasters beside it, with the headline A Kit, Not a Shopping List.
